name: Tufts University
header:
Tufts University
United States · Mathematics PhD
Rank verification is maintained separately.
Eligibility and preparation · Deadlines by stage · English and GRE · Academic records · Recommendation letters · Written
materials · Funding and fees · Conflicts and remaining checks · Faculty · Sources
Pay attention to
• 750-word prompt specifically asks for overcoming an early mathematical challenge.
• Do not submit nonrequired GRE scores; they are not considered.
• Conditional 2-week reference allowance is not guaranteed.
• Loring Tu and Richard Weiss appear on the algebra research page but the current personnel roster lists them
as emeriti. Do not treat them as ordinary new PhD advisers. The core-faculty list also includes postdoctoral
fellows; Raha is explicitly marked as such here.
• Faculty below form a verified research-fit shortlist, not a complete census. New-student supervision and 2027
leave/moves must be confirmed; paper dates describe the cited version.

sections.title: Eligibility and preparation
sections.text:
Eligibility for your route [Standing rule]
Bachelor's by enrollment qualifies; master's not required. No general minimum GPA cutoff. [s4]
Before submission [Standing rule]
Prepare math-specific 750-word statement. Register referees early; request aid in scholarship section; request
fee waiver through admissions if needed. [s1] [s4]
Adviser contact [Standing rule]
No adviser agreement needed before applying; faculty contact recommended to assess fit. [s4]
Portal workflow [Standing rule]
gradase.admissions.tufts.edu. FAQ documents invitation trigger and English-waiver processing; portal-specific
prompts not accessed. [s4]
Cycle verification [Standing rule]
Current pages include 2027 general changes, but mathematics deadline itself is yearless. [s1] [s2]

sections.title: Deadlines by stage
sections.text:
Academic application [Standing rule]
December 1 final fall deadline; page does not explicitly attach 2026/2027 year or cutoff timezone. Confirm
2027 portal. [s1]
Funding consideration [Standing rule]
Aid request is in application; no separate mathematics funding deadline verified. [s4]
Reference receipt [Standing rule]
Aim for December 1. Up to 2 weeks afterward may be allowed depending on departmental review; do not
assume unconditional December 15 extension. [s2] [s4]
Test-score receipt [Standing rule]
Official required scores may be accepted up to 2 weeks after deadline depending on review. Send earlier;
UChicago student route normally exempts English. [s3] [s4]

Supporting documents [Standing rule]
Application complete at program deadline; only letters/test scores have public conditional 2-week receipt
allowance. Final official transcripts due August 1 under FAQ. [s2] [s4]
Accepting an offer [Standing rule]
International page says April 15 for fall confirmation/deposit; exact 2027 offer controls. [s3]

sections.title: English and GRE
sections.text:
English requirement [Standing rule]
Tests generally advised minima: TOEFL 90/4.5, IELTS 6.5, DET 120. Official provider delivery required if testing.
[s3]
UChicago English exemption [Standing rule]
Yes if full-time enrolled in a U.S. degree and 2 consecutive academic years completed before Tufts enrollment;
completed U.S. degree also qualifies. Waiver normally processed within 48 hours after application submission.
[s3] [s4]
GRE General [Standing rule]
Not required/listed for math. General rule: nonrequired GRE scores should not be submitted and are not
considered. [s1] [s4]
GRE Mathematics [Standing rule]
Not required/listed for math. General rule excludes nonrequired GRE scores from consideration. [s1] [s4]

sections.title: Written materials
sections.text:
Academic CV / resume [Standing rule]
Required upload: education/employment dates, honors, scholarships, publications, activities. No math-specific
page/file limit public. [s1] [s2]
Statement of purpose [Standing rule]
Required Personal Statement, max 750 words (overrides generic 2500-word maximum). Prompt paraphrase:
why Tufts/math; what excites you; an early-undergraduate mathematical difficulty, how you overcame it
with/without help, and present understanding. Basic-calculus examples welcome. Upload. [s1]
Personal / background statement [Standing rule]
The math-specific Personal Statement above combines purpose and development. Separate background essay
not listed. [s1]
Research-interest statement [Standing rule]
May discuss within statement; separate document not listed. [s1]
Research proposal; Writing sample / thesis / research summary; Publications list; Course-list
document; Scholarship essays; Other short answers / materials [Unresolved]
The public mathematics and graduate-admissions pages checked do not establish a separate requirement or
permission to submit this item. Required/optional status, exact prompt, length, formatting and
upload-versus-link instructions remain unverified; check the current portal before drafting or sending an extra
document. [s1] [s2] [s3]

sections.title: Funding and fees
sections.text:
Amount and coverage [Unresolved]
Tuition scholarship fully covers GSAS PhD tuition. Math TA/fellowships available, but exact math stipend and
12-month/summer guarantee not verified. Health insurance/wellness fully subsidized 5 years and eligible sixth.
[s5] [s6]
Years of support [Unresolved]
Health coverage 5 years/eligible sixth; math stipend guarantee duration must be confirmed. [s6]
International eligibility [Standing rule]
International TAs generally require spoken-English proficiency or prior U.S.-university training. UChicago may
support this route, but appointment requires department determination. [s8]
Conditions and duties [Standing rule]
TA service and renewal conditions in appointment; degree progress/teaching requirement. [s5] [s8]
Extra funding application [Standing rule]
Request aid through scholarship section of admission application. [s4]
Other funding routes [Standing rule]
Dean's Fellowship adds total USD 10,000 over first 2 years; faculty consider doctoral candidates without
nationality exclusion. No guaranteed award. [s7]
Application fee [Standing rule]
USD 85, credit card or U.S.-bank e-check. [s2]

Fee waiver [Standing rule]
Domestic and international hardship requests accepted case-by-case via linked request form with
documentation. Math department cannot grant/request waiver; Graduate Admissions handles it. [s4] [s5]

sections.title: Potential advisers and recent research
sections.text:
Algebraic / arithmetic geometry
Montserrat Teixidor i Bigas
Algebraic curves, vector bundles and moduli, Brill-Noether theory and limit linear series. [faculty1] [faculty1a]
Current faculty; new PhD supervision availability unconfirmed.
Research evidence: 2026 · Some reducible and irreducible Brill-Noether loci
Official publication evidence for the stated research match.
David Smyth
Official profile emphasizes singular curves and modular compactifications. A verified 2026 publication instead
concerns Boolean reducibility in philosophy; obtain an updated algebraic-geometry project list before assessing
current fit. [faculty3] [faculty3a]
Current faculty; new PhD supervision availability unconfirmed.
Research evidence: 2026 · Supervenience and Boolean Reduction
Official publication evidence for the stated research match.
Neelarnab Raha
Brill-Noether theory of bundles on surfaces, algebraic hyperbolicity and nef cones of Hilbert schemes, including
K3 surfaces. [faculty11] [faculty11a]
Norbert Wiener Fellow, a postdoctoral appointment; useful research contact, not assumed available as a primary long-term PhD
adviser.
Research evidence: 2025 preprint · Nef cones of Hilbert schemes of points on some K3 surfaces
Official publication evidence for the stated research match.
Complex geometry
Charles Cifarelli
Kähler geometry, Kähler-Ricci flow and solitons, Calabi-Yau metrics and weighted K-stability. [faculty5] [faculty5a]
Assistant Professor joining Tufts in Fall 2026; former Stony Brook appointment on publication repository is historical. New-student
availability unconfirmed.
Research evidence: 2026 · On finite time type I singularities of the Kähler-Ricci flow on compact Kähler surfaces
Official publication evidence for the stated research match.

Representation theory
George McNinch
Linear algebraic groups and their representations, Levi factors, nilpotent orbits and local-global principles; also
formalization in Lean. [faculty7] [faculty7a]
Current faculty; new PhD supervision availability unconfirmed.
Research evidence: 2026 preprint · Local-global principles for the existence of Levi factors
Official publication evidence for the stated research match.
Fulton Gonzalez
Lie-group harmonic analysis, symmetric spaces and integral geometry; recent work on wave-equation
reconstruction including noncompact symmetric spaces. [faculty9] [faculty9a]
Current faculty; new PhD supervision availability unconfirmed.
Research evidence: 2024 · The snapshot problem for the wave equation
Official publication evidence for the stated research match.
